application_guidance.input_pattern: A normalized game with exact two-sided feedback, full-gap output and dimensions above the corresponding hard-core threshold.
read_original_when: Changing confidence, expected-cost versus hard-cap accounting, precision, output metric or strategy domain.
Using the adaptive-core argument as a proved interface rather than a literature claim subject to verification.
sensitive_conditions: Ball and simplex normalization and dimension/log conditions must not be merged.
The game query is joint; its reduction costs two ordinary source-system matvecs.
Small primal objective alone is not a replacement for the required full-gap guarantee in an altered problem.
Auxiliary Haar sampling is internal to the simplex reduction, not a universal game hard distribution.
Any matrix can be reconstructed in at most min(m,n) two-sided basis queries, so the displayed accuracy lower bounds cannot hold uniformly in fixed small dimensions.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Success at least 2/3 on every admissible fixed matrix; almost-sure hard query cap on every transcript.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Universal constants and sufficiently-large/small thresholds; no matching logarithms or full joint characterization in (m,n,epsilon).
complexity_scope.oracle: One joint arbitrary-real-vector query returns (Ax,A^T y). This is not two charged game queries.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Feasible primal-dual strategy pair and full saddle-point gap, separately defined for each geometry.
complexity_scope.regime: Sufficiently large N in the sequence theorem or sufficiently small epsilon in the corollary; ball dimensions m>=4N,n>=2N+1; simplex dimensions m,n>=4N, with different N(epsilon).
complexity_scope.resource: Joint exact game-matvec count only; no runtime, memory, communication, precision or parallel-depth lower bound.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Arbitrary measurable randomized adaptive exact-matvec algorithms, including arbitrary feasible outputs; fixed worst-case instance for each algorithm, independent of its realized seed.

content.intended_use: Use the selected literature lower-bound statement with explicit geometry, dimension, probability and query-accounting conditions.

map: Import Theorem 4.1: for k>=1,0<s<=1, standard real Gin(k) has c_he s<=P(sigma_min<=s/sqrt(k))<=C_he s. Import Proposition 4.2 Gaussian operator-norm tail. External originals are not reverified here.

Lemmas 5.1–5.3 and Theorem 5.4 retain the complete two-sided adaptive transcript and extract a fresh ell×ell Gaussian core, ell=N−4t>=N/2 for t<=N/8. Uniform conditional small-singular-value probability plus an unconditional separated high event forces a universal factor-two estimation failure floor gamma>0. See the batch proof_method for the source-linked extraction map.

Theorem 6.5 uses H in H_{d,kappa}={H=H^T:sigma_min(H)>=1,||H||op<=kappa}, d=2N,kappa=CN. A source solver must handle every right-hand side and achieve residual <=||r||_2/2 with probability >=3/5. Set H=(sqrt(N)/a_star)[0,G;G^T,0]. One H matvec costs one joint Gaussian query. Outside the source promise retain a hard cap and default output. Hard-edge and norm tails make promise failure small relative to gamma.

Lemmas 6.2–6.4 amplify each source correction using fresh independent seeds and exact residual verification, costing R(K+1); reuse verification products in refinement. J=O(log N) corrections give inverse applications of accuracy eta=Theta(1/(sqrt(N)log N)). O(log N) inverse-power steps and a constant number of Haar starts estimate ||H^{-1}|| within factor two. R=O(log log N) repetitions cover O(log^2 N) adaptively generated correction calls by conditioning on their histories. Total <=C'(K+1)log^2(N+2)log log(N+e^e) joint Gaussian queries contradict Theorem 5.4 when too small. Hence K=Omega(N/[log^2(N+2)log log(N+e^e)]).

Ball–simplex §7.1: for unit b, d=2N, beta=1/(4kappa), alpha=beta/(8sqrt(d)), define C_(i,sigma),:=alpha e_{d+1}^T+sigma beta(e_i^T H,−b_i), A=−C. Rows have norm <1. With w=(z,s), psi=alpha s−beta||Hz−sb||_infinity. The feasible homogeneous solution witness gives game value <=−alpha/sqrt(2). Full gap <=alpha/16 forces s>=1/sqrt(2)−1/16>0 and ||H(z/s)−b||_2<1/2. Arbitrary joint game feedback is simulated using Hz and H(y_plus−y_minus): TWO ordinary H matvecs. Nonunit RHS is normalized and output rescaled; zero RHS returns zero. Thus success >=2/3 gives a 3/5 source solver at cost 2T, and alpha/16=Theta(N^(−3/2)).

Simplex–simplex §7.2: take independent Haar Q, R=sqrt(d)[Q,−Q], V=sqrt(d)[I,−I], Lambda=C_emb kappa sqrt(d log(d+2)), A=[R^T HV−(R^T b)1^T]/Lambda. Lemma 7.5 gives entrywise admissibility with probability >=0.99 for each fixed H and unit b. A simplex witness represents H^{-1}b using V and satisfies Ax_star=0. The signed testing dictionary gives max_i(R^T z)_i>=||z||_2, hence full gap >=||HVx−b||_2/Lambda for every feasible pair. Gap <=1/(2Lambda) yields half residual. A joint game query uses H(Vx),H(Ry), TWO ordinary H matvecs; retain 1^T x in the feedback formula for arbitrary real queries. Per-admissible-game success and independent Q give source success >=0.99*(2/3)>3/5. Lambda=Theta(N^(3/2)sqrt(log N)) supplies the second accuracy sequence.

Corollary 3.3 proof p.21: both accuracy sequences decrease eventually with consecutive ratio tending to one. Choose epsilon_{N+1}<epsilon<=epsilon_N. Success at epsilon implies success at epsilon_N. Invert the two sequences separately; log N=Theta(log(1/epsilon)), and the simplex N contributes the extra log^(1/3) factor. Lemma 3.4 extends the core dimensions by exact geometry-specific padding.
proofs.omitted_details: Long literature proof is preserved as a source-linked map, not an independent reproof. External random-matrix results and inherited deterministic upper bounds are not independently verified. No new local proof is substituted for the source's qualified adaptive-core argument.
proofs.reading_coverage: Read complete statements, query convention, §5 posterior/core proof, §6 solver reduction, §7 embeddings and proof of Corollary 3.3; visually checked initial pp.5–11. Source's §8 verification qualification retained.

assumptions: Queries may use arbitrary real vectors and return (Ax,A^T y) jointly for ONE query. Only outputs must belong to the corresponding strategy domains.
Algorithms may be randomized and adaptive without a Krylov/span restriction; private randomness is independent of the fixed input matrix.
An at-most-T budget means an almost-sure hard cap on every transcript, including off-promise transcripts. Exact arithmetic and internal computation are unrestricted and uncharged.
Natural logarithms; all constants in the statements below are universal; dimensions and accuracy must satisfy the geometry-specific regime.
statement.conclusion: At either sequence accuracy, every qualifying algorithm needs at least c2 N/[log^2(N+2) log log(N+e^e)] joint queries. Consequently in the respective Corollary 3.3 regimes, Q_rand^{2,1}(m,n,epsilon)>=Omega(epsilon^(−2/3)/[log^2(1/epsilon) log log(1/epsilon)]) and Q_rand^{1,1}(m,n,epsilon)>=Omega(epsilon^(−2/3)/[log^(7/3)(1/epsilon) log log(1/epsilon)]). These are the selected manuscript's literature claims, subject to its explicit proof-verification qualification.
statement.objects_and_definitions: A in R^{m×n}; x minimizes and y maximizes y^T Ax. Delta_k={z>=0:1^T z=1}, B_2^k={z:||z||_2<=1}. Ball–simplex: x in B_2^n,y in Delta_m, max_i||A_i,:||_2<=1, Gap_A^{2,1}=max_i(Ax)_i+||A^T y||_2. Simplex–simplex: x in Delta_n,y in Delta_m, max_ij|A_ij|<=1, Gap_A^{1,1}=max_i(Ax)_i−min_j(A^T y)_j. Q_rand^{2,1} and Q_rand^{1,1} are the minimum worst-case counts of exact two-sided joint queries needed to return feasible pairs of gap at most epsilon with success probability at least 2/3 on every admissible matrix.
statement.parameter_domains: Theorem 3.2: ball–simplex (m_N,n_N)=(4N,2N+1), epsilon_N=c0/N^(3/2); simplex–simplex (m_N,n_N)=(4N,4N), epsilon_N=c1/[N^(3/2)sqrt(log(N+2))]. For Corollary 3.3 choose N by epsilon_{N+1}<epsilon<=epsilon_N in the relevant sequence: ball N=Theta(epsilon^(−2/3)), m>=4N,n>=2N+1; simplex N=Theta(epsilon^(−2/3)/log^(1/3)(1/epsilon)), m,n>=4N.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist universal c0,c1,c2>0 such that for every sufficiently large integer N the sequence bounds hold. Equivalently, every randomized algorithm below the lower threshold fails the 2/3 requirement on some fixed admissible matrix; that matrix may depend on the algorithm but not its realized private seed. No universal Yao distribution over games is asserted. Corollary bounds hold for every sufficiently small epsilon with the selected corresponding N and all dimensions above the stated thresholds.
